title: How the Story Feels with Author’s Tone?
use_cases: Use when differentiating between Epic Fantasy and Magical Realism through prose style
Implement when crafting a serious, myth-like atmosphere for world-building
Configure when seeking a matter-of-fact delivery for supernatural elements
Analyze when evaluating how tone affects the reader's perception of magic
content:
How does the author tell the story? The “voice” of the book is a great hint.

Fantasy often has an “epic” tone. The language is big. The stakes are high. The world is in danger. It is serious. It feels like a myth or a legend. This is part of its charm. It makes you feel like you are part of something huge.

Magical realism has a “matter-of-fact” tone. The author uses simple, clear language. They describe an impossible event the same way they would describe making coffee. This plain tone makes the magical event feel even more real. It shocks the reader, but not the characters. This style is a key tool. It helps the blending reality and fantasy feel smooth.

This difference in tone is a major part of the fantasy fiction vs magical realism divide. One shouts about magic. The other whispers about it.
